units.rightText: and Michael, and Ishpah, and Joha, the sons of Beriah,

units.leftText: Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
units.rightText: and Zebadiah, and Meshullam, and Hizki, and Heber,

units.leftText: Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were the sons of Elpaal.
units.rightText: and Ishmerai, and Izliah, and Jobab, the sons of Elpaal,

units.leftText: Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
units.rightText: and Jakim, and Zichri, and Zabdi,

units.leftText: Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
units.rightText: and Elienai, and Zillethai, and Eliel,

units.leftText: Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimei.
units.rightText: and Adaiah, and Beraiah, and Shimrath, the sons of Shimei,

units.leftText: Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
units.rightText: and Ishpan, and Eber, and Eliel,

units.leftText: Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
units.rightText: and Abdon, and Zichri, and Hanan,

units.leftText: Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
units.rightText: and Hananiah, and Elam, and Anthothijah,

units.leftText: Iphdeiah, and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.
units.rightText: and Iphdeiah, and Penuel, the sons of Shashak,

units.leftText: Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
units.rightText: and Shamsherai, and Shehariah, and Athaliah,

units.leftText: Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were the sons of Jeroham.
units.rightText: and Jaareshiah, and Elijah, and Zichri, the sons of Jeroham.

units.leftText: All these were heads of families, the chiefs according to their genealogies, and they lived in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: These were heads of fathers’ houses throughout their generations, chief men: these dwelt in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah,
units.rightText: And in Gibeon there dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jeiel, whose wife’s name was Maacah;
leftNotes: 8:29 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Chronicles 9:35|1CH 9:35*); Hebrew The father of Gibeon lived

units.leftText: and Abdon was his firstborn son, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
units.rightText: and his first-born son Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Nadab,
leftNotes: 8:30 Some LXX manuscripts include Ner; see 1 Chronicles 9:36|1CH 9:36*.

units.leftText: Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
units.rightText: and Gedor, and Ahio, and Zecher.
leftNotes: 8:31 Zecher is likely a variant of Zechariah; see 1 Chronicles 9:37|1CH 9:37*.

units.leftText: and Mikloth, who was the father of Shimeah. They too lived alongside their relatives in Jerusalem. The Family of Saul
units.rightText: And Mikloth begat Shimeah. And they also dwelt with their brethren in Jerusalem, over against their brethren.
leftNotes: 8:32 Shimeah is a variant of Shimeam; see 1 Chronicles 9:38|1CH 9:38*.

units.leftText: Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
units.rightText: And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchi-shua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
leftNotes: 8:33 Esh-baal is also called Ish-bosheth; see 2 Samuel 2:8|2SA 2:8*.

units.leftText: The son of Jonathan: Merib-baal, and Merib-baal was the father of Micah.
units.rightText: And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal begat Micah.
leftNotes: 8:34 Merib-baal is also called Mephibosheth; see 2 Samuel 4:4|2SA 4:4*.
8:34 Micah is a variant of Mica; see 2 Samuel 9:12|2SA 9:12*.

units.leftText: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
units.rightText: And the sons of Micah: Pithon, and Melech, and Tarea, and Ahaz.
leftNotes: 8:35 Tarea is a variant of Tahrea; see 1 Chronicles 9:41|1CH 9:41*.

units.leftText: Ahaz was the father of Jehoaddah, Jehoaddah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri was the father of Moza.
units.rightText: And Ahaz begat Jehoaddah; and Jehoaddah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza.
leftNotes: 8:36 Jehoaddah is a variant of Jarah or Jadah; see 1 Chronicles 9:42|1CH 9:42*.

units.leftText: Moza was the father of Binea. Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
units.rightText: And Moza begat Binea; Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
leftNotes: 8:37 Raphah is a variant of Rephaiah; see 1 Chronicles 9:43|1CH 9:43*.

units.leftText: Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.
units.rightText: And Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.

units.leftText: The sons of his brother Eshek:
units.rightText: And the sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his first-born, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.

units.leftText: The sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers, and they had many sons and grandsons— 150 in all. All these were the descendants of Benjamin.
units.rightText: And the sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons, and sons’ sons, a hundred and fifty. All these were of the sons of Benjamin.

units.leftText: So all Israel was recorded in the genealogies written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. But Judah was exiled to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.
units.rightText: So all Israel were reckoned by genealogies; and, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel. And Judah was carried away captive to Babylon for their transgression.

units.leftText: Now the first to resettle their own property in their cities were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
units.rightText: Now the first inhabitants that dwelt in their possessions in their cities were Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the Nethinim.
leftNotes: 9:2 Hebrew Nethinim

units.leftText: Some of the descendants of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem:
units.rightText: And in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim and Manasseh:

units.leftText: Uthai son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, a descendant of Perez son of Judah.
units.rightText: Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Perez the son of Judah.

units.leftText: From the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.
units.rightText: And of the Shilonites: Asaiah the first-born, and his sons.

units.leftText: From the Zerahites: Jeuel and 690 relatives.
units.rightText: And of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel, and their brethren, six hundred and ninety.

units.leftText: From the Benjamites: Sallu son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah;
units.rightText: And of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah,

units.leftText: Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, the son of Michri; Meshullam son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah;
units.rightText: and Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah;

units.leftText: and 956 of their relatives according to their genealogy. All these men were heads of their families.
units.rightText: and their brethren, according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty and six. All these men were heads of fathers’ houses by their fathers’ houses.

units.leftText: From the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin;
units.rightText: And of the priests: Jedaiah, and Jehoiarib, Jachin,

units.leftText: Azariah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the chief official of God’s temple;
units.rightText: and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of the house of God;

units.leftText: Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah; Maasai son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
units.rightText: and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
leftNotes: 9:12 Meshillemith is a variant of Meshillemoth; see Nehemiah 11:13|NEH 11:13*.

units.leftText: and 1,760 of their relatives, the heads of their families, able men for the work of the service of the house of God.
units.rightText: and their brethren, heads of their fathers’ houses, a thousand and seven hundred and threescore; very able men for the work of the service of the house of God.

units.leftText: From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, a descendant of Merari;
units.rightText: And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;

units.leftText: Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph;
units.rightText: and Bakbakkar, Heresh, and Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph,

units.leftText: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
units.rightText: and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, that dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites.

units.leftText: These were the gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives.
units.rightText: And the porters: Shallum, and Akkub, and Talmon, and Ahiman, and their brethren (Shallum was the chief),

units.leftText: he was previously stationed at the King’s Gate on the east side. These were the gatekeepers from the camp of the Levites.
units.rightText: who hitherto waited in the king’s gate eastward: they were the porters for the camp of the children of Levi.

units.leftText: Shallum son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his relatives from the Korahites were assigned to guard the thresholds of the Tent, just as their fathers had been assigned to guard the entrance to the dwelling of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren, of his father’s house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent: and their fathers had been over the camp of Jehovah, keepers of the entry.
leftNotes: 9:19 Ebiasaph is a variant of Abiasaph; see Exodus 6:24|EXO 6:24*.

units.leftText: In earlier times Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of the gatekeepers, and the LORD was with him.
units.rightText: And Phinehas the son of Eleazar was ruler over them in time past, and Jehovah was with him.

units.leftText: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was porter of the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: The number of those chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds was 212. They were registered by genealogy in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their positions of trust.
units.rightText: All these that were chosen to be porters in the thresholds were two hundred and twelve. These were reckoned by genealogy in their villages, whom David and Samuel the seer did ordain in their office of trust.

units.leftText: So they and their descendants were assigned to guard the gates of the house of the LORD — the house called the Tent.
units.rightText: So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the house of Jehovah, even the house of the tent, by wards.

units.leftText: The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides: east, west, north, and south.
units.rightText: On the four sides were the porters, toward the east, west, north, and south.

units.leftText: Their relatives came from their villages at fixed times to serve with them for seven-day periods.
units.rightText: And their brethren, in their villages, were to come in every seven days from time to time to be with them:

units.leftText: But the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were entrusted with the rooms and the treasuries of the house of God.
units.rightText: for the four chief porters, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and were over the chambers and over the treasuries in the house of God.

units.leftText: They would spend the night stationed around the house of God, because they were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning.
units.rightText: And they lodged round about the house of God, because the charge thereof was upon them; and to them pertained the opening thereof morning by morning.

units.leftText: Some of them were in charge of the articles used in worship, to count them whenever they were brought in or taken out.
units.rightText: And certain of them had charge of the vessels of service; for by count were these brought in and by count were these taken out.

units.leftText: Others were put in charge of the furnishings and other articles of the sanctuary, as well as the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
units.rightText: Some of them also were appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, and over the fine flour, and the wine, and the oil, and the frankincense, and the spices.

units.leftText: And some of the sons of the priests mixed the spices.
units.rightText: And some of the sons of the priests prepared the confection of the spices.

units.leftText: A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with baking the bread.
units.rightText: And Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the first-born of Shallum the Korahite, had the office of trust over the things that were baked in pans.

units.leftText: Some of their Kohathite relatives were responsible for preparing the rows of the showbread every Sabbath.
units.rightText: And some of their brethren, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the showbread, to prepare it every sabbath.

units.leftText: Those who were musicians, the heads of Levite families, stayed in the temple chambers and were exempt from other duties because they were on duty day and night.
units.rightText: And these are the singers, heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites, who dwelt in the chambers and were free from other service; for they were employed in their work day and night.

units.leftText: All these were heads of Levite families, chiefs according to their genealogies, and they lived in Jerusalem. The Descendants of Saul
units.rightText: These were heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites, throughout their generations, chief men: these dwelt at Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah.
units.rightText: And in Gibeon there dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jeiel, whose wife’s name was Maacah;
leftNotes: 9:35 Or the founder

units.leftText: Abdon was his firstborn son, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
units.rightText: and his first-born son Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab,

units.leftText: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
units.rightText: and Gedor, and Ahio, and Zechariah, and Mikloth.

units.leftText: Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They too lived alongside their relatives in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And Mikloth begat Shimeam. And they also dwelt with their brethren in Jerusalem, over against their brethren.
leftNotes: 9:38 Shimeam is a variant of Shimeah; see 1 Chronicles 8:32|1CH 8:32*.

units.leftText: Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
units.rightText: And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.

units.leftText: The son of Jonathan: Merib-baal, who was the father of Micah.
units.rightText: And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal begat Micah.

units.leftText: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
units.rightText: And the sons of Micah: Pithon, and Melech, and Tahrea, and Ahaz.
leftNotes: 9:41 Vulgate and Syriac (see also LXX and 1 Chronicles 8:35|1CH 8:35*); Hebrew Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea; note that Tahrea is a variant of Tarea.

units.leftText: Ahaz was the father of Jarah; Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri was the father of Moza.
units.rightText: And Ahaz begat Jarah; and Jarah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza;
leftNotes: 9:42 Most Hebrew manuscripts; some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX Jadah; Jadah; note that Jarah and Jadah are variants of Jehoaddah; see 1 Chronicles 8:36|1CH 8:36*.

units.leftText: Moza was the father of Binea. Rephaiah was his son, Elasah his son, and Azel his son.
units.rightText: and Moza begat Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
leftNotes: 9:43 Rephaiah is a variant of Raphah; see 1 Chronicles 8:37|1CH 8:37*.

units.leftText: And Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.
units.rightText: And Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan: these were the sons of Azel.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.

units.leftText: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
units.rightText: And the Philistines followed hard after Saul and after his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.

units.leftText: When the battle intensified against Saul, the archers overtook him and wounded him.
units.rightText: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he was distressed by reason of the archers.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised men will come and torture me!” But his armor-bearer was terrified and refused to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
units.rightText: Then said Saul unto his armor-bearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith, lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me. But his armor-bearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took his sword, and fell upon it.

units.leftText: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died.
units.rightText: And when his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he likewise fell upon his sword, and died.

units.leftText: So Saul died together with his three sons and all his house. The Philistines Possess the Towns (1 Samuel 31:7–10|1SA 31:7-10*)
units.rightText: So Saul died, and his three sons; and all his house died together.

units.leftText: When all the Israelites in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their cities and ran away. So the Philistines came and occupied their cities.
units.rightText: And when all the men of Israel that were in the valley saw that they fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook their cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

units.leftText: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his sons fallen in mount Gilboa.

units.leftText: They stripped Saul, cut off his head, took his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temple of their idols and among their people.
units.rightText: And they stripped him, and took his head, and his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to carry the tidings unto their idols, and to the people.

units.leftText: They put his armor in the temple of their gods and hung his head in the temple of Dagon. Jabesh-gilead’s Tribute to Saul (1 Samuel 31:11–13|1SA 31:11-13*)
units.rightText: And they put his armor in the house of their gods, and fastened his head in the house of Dagon.

units.leftText: When all the people of Jabesh-gilead heard about everything the Philistines had done to Saul,
units.rightText: And when all Jabesh-gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul,

units.leftText: all their men of valor set out and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh. And they buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fasted seven days.
units.rightText: all the valiant men arose, and took away the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh, and buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
leftNotes: 10:12 Or terebinth or great tree

units.leftText: So Saul died for his unfaithfulness to the LORD, because he did not keep the word of the LORD and even consulted a medium for guidance,
units.rightText: So Saul died for his trespass which he committed against Jehovah, because of the word of Jehovah, which he kept not; and also for that he asked counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to inquire thereby,

units.leftText: and he failed to inquire of the LORD. So the LORD put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.
units.rightText: and inquired not of Jehovah: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.

units.leftText: Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron and said, “Here we are, your own flesh and blood.
units.rightText: Then all Israel gathered themselves to David unto Hebron, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.

units.leftText: Even in times past, while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them back. And the LORD your God said, ‘You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them.’”
units.rightText: In times past, even when Saul was king, it was thou that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and Jehovah thy God said unto thee, Thou shalt be shepherd of my people Israel, and thou shalt be prince over my people Israel.
leftNotes: 11:2 Or For some time

units.leftText: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, where David made a covenant with them before the LORD. And they anointed him king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD through Samuel. David Conquers Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:6–11|2SA 5:6-11*)
units.rightText: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Jehovah; and they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of Jehovah by Samuel.

units.leftText: Then David and all the Israelites marched to Jerusalem (that is, Jebus), where the Jebusites inhabited the land.
units.rightText: And David and all Israel went to Jerusalem (the same is Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were there.

units.leftText: The people of Jebus said to David, “You will never get in here.” Nevertheless , David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).
units.rightText: And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, Thou shalt not come in hither. Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion; the same is the city of David.

units.leftText: Now David had said, “Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander.” And Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became the chief.
units.rightText: And David said, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain. And Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, and was made chief.

units.leftText: So David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David.
units.rightText: And David dwelt in the stronghold; therefore they called it the city of David.

units.leftText: He built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall, while Joab restored the rest of the city.
units.rightText: And he built the city round about, from Millo even round about; and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
leftNotes: 11:8 Hebrew the Millo

units.leftText: And David became greater and greater, for the LORD of Hosts was with him. David’s Mighty Men (2 Samuel 23:8–39|2SA 23:8-39*)
units.rightText: And David waxed greater and greater; for Jehovah of hosts was with him.

units.leftText: Now these were the chiefs of David’s mighty men, who, together with all Israel, bolstered and strengthened his kingdom, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.
units.rightText: Now these are the chief of the mighty men whom David had, who showed themselves strong with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of Jehovah concerning Israel.

units.leftText: This is the list of David’s mighty men: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni was chief of the officers; he wielded his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed at one time.
units.rightText: And this is the number of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them at one time.
leftNotes: 11:11 Or of the Thirty; some LXX manuscripts of the Three; see 2 Samuel 23:8|2SA 23:8*.

units.leftText: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.
units.rightText: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, who was one of the three mighty men.
leftNotes: 11:12 Dodo is a variant of Dodai; see 1 Chronicles 27:4|1CH 27:4*.

units.leftText: He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. At a place with a field full of barley, the troops fled from the Philistines.
units.rightText: He was with David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where was a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.

units.leftText: But Eleazar and David stationed themselves in the middle of the field and defended it. They struck down the Philistines, and the LORD brought about a great victory.
units.rightText: And they stood in the midst of the plot, and defended it, and slew the Philistines; and Jehovah saved them by a great victory.
leftNotes: 11:14 Literally But they stationed themselves

units.leftText: Three of the thirty chief men went down to David, to the rock at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: And three of the thirty chief men went down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the host of the Philistines were encamped in the valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.
units.rightText: And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Beth-lehem.

units.leftText: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”
units.rightText: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me water to drink of the well of Beth-lehem, which is by the gate!

units.leftText: So the Three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well at the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead , he poured it out to the LORD,
units.rightText: And the three brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Beth-lehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: but David would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto Jehovah,

units.leftText: saying, “Far be it from me, my God, to do this! How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?” Because they had brought it at the risk of their lives, David refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.
units.rightText: and said, My God forbid it me, that I should do this: shall I drink the blood of these men that have put their lives in jeopardy? for with the jeopardy of their lives they brought it. Therefore he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty men.

units.leftText: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the Three, and he wielded his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.
units.rightText: And Abishai, the brother of Joab, he was chief of the three; for he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them, and had a name among the three.
leftNotes: 11:20 Hebrew; Syriac the Thirty; also in verse 21

units.leftText: He was doubly honored above the Three, and he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.
units.rightText: Of the three, he was more honorable than the two, and was made their captain: howbeit he attained not to the first three.

units.leftText: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
units.rightText: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds, he slew the two sons of Ariel of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow.
leftNotes: 11:22 Or two sons of Ariel of Moab

units.leftText: He also struck down an Egyptian, a huge man five cubits tall. Although the Egyptian had a spear like a weaver’s beam in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.
units.rightText: And he slew an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high; and in the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and slew him with his own spear.
leftNotes: 11:23 5 cubits is approximately 7 feet 6 inches or 229 centimeters tall.

units.leftText: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name along with the three mighty men.
units.rightText: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had a name among the three mighty men.

units.leftText: He was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three. And David appointed him over his guard.
units.rightText: Behold, he was more honorable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three: and David set him over his guard.

units.leftText: Now these were the mighty men: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
units.rightText: Also the mighty men of the armies: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Beth-lehem,

units.leftText: Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
units.rightText: Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
leftNotes: 11:27 Shammoth the Harorite is a variant of Shammah the Harodite; see 2 Samuel 23:25|2SA 23:25*.

units.leftText: Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,
units.rightText: Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,

units.leftText: Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
units.rightText: Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,

units.leftText: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,
units.rightText: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite,

units.leftText: Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjamites, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
units.rightText: Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
leftNotes: 11:31 Ithai is a variant of Ittai; see 2 Samuel 23:29|2SA 23:29*.

units.leftText: Hurai from the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
units.rightText: Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
leftNotes: 11:32 Hurai is a variant of Hiddai; see 2 Samuel 23:30|2SA 23:30*.
11:32 Or from the ravines
11:32 Abiel is a variant of Abi-albon; see 2 Samuel 23:31|2SA 23:31*.

units.leftText: Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
units.rightText: Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
leftNotes: 11:33 Baharumite is a variant of Barhumite; see 2 Samuel 23:31|2SA 23:31*.

units.leftText: the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite,
units.rightText: the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite,
leftNotes: 11:34 Hashem is a variant of Jashen; see LXX and 2 Samuel 23:32|2SA 23:32*.

units.leftText: Ahiam son of Sachar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,
units.rightText: Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur,
leftNotes: 11:35 Sachar is a variant of Sharar; see 2 Samuel 23:33|2SA 23:33*.

units.leftText: Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,
units.rightText: Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,

units.leftText: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai,
units.rightText: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai,

units.leftText: Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar son of Hagri,
units.rightText: Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri,

units.leftText: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
units.rightText: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armorbearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,

units.leftText: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
units.rightText: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

units.leftText: Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai,
units.rightText: Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai,

units.leftText: Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, chief of the Reubenites, and the thirty with him,
units.rightText: Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,

units.leftText: Hanan son of Maacah, Joshaphat the Mithnite,
units.rightText: Hanan the son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,

units.leftText: Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,
units.rightText: Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,

units.leftText: Jediael son of Shimri and his brother Joha the Tizite,
units.rightText: Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,

units.leftText: Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite,
units.rightText: Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,

units.leftText: Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
units.rightText: Eliel, and Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

units.leftText: Now these were the men who came to David at Ziklag, while he was still banished from the presence of Saul son of Kish (they were among the mighty men who helped him in battle;
units.rightText: Now these are they that came to David to Ziklag, while he yet kept himself close because of Saul the son of Kish; and they were among the mighty men, his helpers in war.

units.leftText: they were archers using both the right and left hands to sling stones and shoot arrows; and they were Saul’s kinsmen from Benjamin):
units.rightText: They were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and in shooting arrows from the bow: they were of Saul’s brethren of Benjamin.

units.leftText: Ahiezer their chief and Joash, who were the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu the Anathothite;
units.rightText: The chief was Ahiezer; then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite, and Jeziel, and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth, and Beracah, and Jehu the Anathothite,

units.leftText: Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the Thirty and a leader over the Thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite;
units.rightText: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty, and Jeremiah, and Jahaziel, and Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite,

units.leftText: Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite;
units.rightText: Eluzai, and Jerimoth, and Bealiah, and Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite,

units.leftText: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, who were Korahites;
units.rightText: Elkanah, and Isshiah, and Azarel, and Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites,

units.leftText: and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.
units.rightText: and Joelah, and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.

units.leftText: Some Gadites defected to David at his stronghold in the wilderness. They were mighty men of valor, trained for battle, experts with the shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains:
units.rightText: And of the Gadites there separated themselves unto David to the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, that could handle shield and spear; whose faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as swift as the roes upon the mountains:

units.leftText: Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second in command, Eliab the third,
units.rightText: Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,

units.leftText: Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
units.rightText: Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,

units.leftText: Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
units.rightText: Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,

units.leftText: Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
units.rightText: Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,

units.leftText: Jeremiah the tenth, and Machbanai the eleventh.
units.rightText: Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.

units.leftText: These Gadites were army commanders, the least of whom was a match for a hundred, and the greatest for a thousand.
units.rightText: These of the sons of Gad were captains of the host: he that was least was equal to a hundred, and the greatest to a thousand.

units.leftText: These are the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month when it was overflowing all its banks, and they put to flight all those in the valleys, both to the east and to the west.
units.rightText: These are they that went over the Jordan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toward the east and toward the west.

units.leftText: Other Benjamites and some men from Judah also came to David in his stronghold.
units.rightText: And there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the stronghold unto David.

units.leftText: And David went out to meet them, saying, “If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my enemies when my hands are free of violence, may the God of our fathers see it and judge you.”
units.rightText: And David went out to meet them, and answered and said unto them, If ye be come peaceably unto me to help me, my heart shall be knit unto you; but if ye be come to betray me to mine adversaries, seeing there is no wrong in my hands, the God of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it.

units.leftText: Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, and he said: “We are yours, O David! We are with you, O son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers, for your God helps you.” So David received them and made them leaders of his troops.
units.rightText: Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, who was chief of the thirty, and he said, Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse: peace, peace be unto thee, and peace be to thy helpers; for thy God helpeth thee. Then David received them, and made them captains of the band.

units.leftText: Some from Manasseh defected to David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. (They did not help the Philistines because the Philistine rulers consulted and sent David away, saying, “It will cost us our heads if he defects to his master Saul.”)
units.rightText: Of Manasseh also there fell away some to David, when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle: but they helped them not; for the lords of the Philistines upon advisement sent him away, saying, He will fall away to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our heads.

units.leftText: When David went to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh defected to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of thousands in Manasseh.
units.rightText: As he went to Ziklag, there fell to him of Manasseh, Adnah, and Jozabad, and Jediael, and Michael, and Jozabad, and Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands that were of Manasseh.

units.leftText: They helped David against the raiders, for they were all mighty men of valor and commanders in the army.
units.rightText: And they helped David against the band of rovers: for they were all mighty men of valor, and were captains in the host.

units.leftText: For at that time men came to David day after day to help him, until he had a great army, like the army of God. David’s Army Grows at Hebron
units.rightText: For from day to day men came to David to help him, until there was a great host, like the host of God.

units.leftText: Now these are the numbers of men armed for battle who came to David at Hebron to turn Saul’s kingdom over to him, in accordance with the word of the LORD:
units.rightText: And these are the numbers of the heads of them that were armed for war, who came to David to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of Jehovah.

units.leftText: From Judah: 6,800 armed troops bearing shields and spears.
units.rightText: The children of Judah that bare shield and spear were six thousand and eight hundred, armed for war.

units.leftText: From Simeon: 7,100 mighty men of valor, ready for battle.
units.rightText: Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the war, seven thousand and one hundred.

units.leftText: From Levi: 4,600,
units.rightText: Of the children of Levi four thousand and six hundred.

units.leftText: including Jehoiada, leader of the house of Aaron, with 3,700 men,
units.rightText: And Jehoiada was the leader of the house of Aaron; and with him were three thousand and seven hundred,

units.leftText: and Zadok, a mighty young man of valor, with 22 commanders from his own family.
units.rightText: and Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father’s house twenty and two captains.

units.leftText: From Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul: 3,000, most of whom had remained loyal to the house of Saul up to that time.
units.rightText: And of the children of Benjamin, the brethren of Saul, three thousand: for hitherto the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to the house of Saul.

units.leftText: From Ephraim: 20,800 mighty men of valor, famous among their own clans.
units.rightText: And of the children of Ephraim twenty thousand and eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers’ houses.

units.leftText: From the half-tribe of Manasseh: 18,000 designated by name to come and make David king.
units.rightText: And of the half-tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, who were mentioned by name, to come and make David king.
leftNotes: 12:31 That is, the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan

units.leftText: From Issachar, men who understood the times and knew what Israel should do: 200 chiefs with all their kinsmen at their command.
units.rightText: And of the children of Issachar, men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.

units.leftText: From Zebulun: 50,000 fit for service, trained for battle with all kinds of weapons of war, who with one purpose were devoted to David.
units.rightText: Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the host, that could set the battle in array, with all manner of instruments of war, fifty thousand, and that could order the battle array, and were not of double heart.
leftNotes: 12:33 LXX; Hebrew does not include to David.

units.leftText: From Naphtali: 1,000 commanders, accompanied by 37,000 men with shield and spear.
units.rightText: And of Naphtali a thousand captains, and with them with shield and spear thirty and seven thousand.

units.leftText: From Dan: 28,600 prepared for battle.
units.rightText: And of the Danites that could set the battle in array, twenty and eight thousand and six hundred.

units.leftText: From Asher: 40,000 fit for service, prepared for battle.
units.rightText: And of Asher, such as were able to go out in the host, that could set the battle in array, forty thousand.

units.leftText: And from east of the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh there: 120,000 armed with every kind of weapon of war.
units.rightText: And on the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all manner of instruments of war for the battle, a hundred and twenty thousand.

units.leftText: All these men of war, arrayed for battle, came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of the Israelites were of one mind to make David king.
units.rightText: All these, being men of war, that could order the battle array, came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.

units.leftText: They spent three days there eating and drinking with David, for their relatives had provided for them.
units.rightText: And they were there with David three days, eating and drinking; for their brethren had made preparation for them.

units.leftText: And their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali came bringing food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen— abundant supplies of flour, fig cakes and raisin cakes, wine and oil, oxen and sheep. Indeed, there was joy in Israel.
units.rightText: Moreover they that were nigh unto them, even as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, brought bread on asses, and on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, victuals of meal, cakes of figs, and clusters of raisins, and wine, and oil, and oxen, and sheep in abundance: for there was joy in Israel.

units.leftText: Then David conferred with all his leaders, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.
units.rightText: And David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, even with every leader.

units.leftText: And he said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if this is of the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to the rest of our brothers in all the land of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in their cities and pasturelands, so that they may join us.
units.rightText: And David said unto all the assembly of Israel, If it seem good unto you, and if it be of Jehovah our God, let us send abroad every where unto our brethren that are left in all the land of Israel, with whom the priests and Levites are in their cities that have suburbs, that they may gather themselves unto us;

units.leftText: Then let us bring back the ark of our God, for we did not inquire of Him in the days of Saul.”
units.rightText: and let us bring again the ark of our God to us: for we sought not unto it in the days of Saul.
leftNotes: 13:3 Or of it

units.leftText: And because this proposal seemed right to all the people, the whole assembly agreed to it.
units.rightText: And all the assembly said that they would do so; for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.

units.leftText: So David assembled all Israel, from the River Shihor in Egypt to Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
units.rightText: So David assembled all Israel together, from the Shihor the brook of Egypt even unto the entrance of Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
leftNotes: 13:5 Hebrew from the Shihor

units.leftText: David and all Israel went up to Baalah of Judah (that is, Kiriath-jearim) to bring up from there the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim — the ark that is called by the Name.
units.rightText: And David went up, and all Israel, to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath-jearim, which belonged to Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God Jehovah that sitteth above the cherubim, that is called by the Name.
leftNotes: 13:6 Or the ark of God, which is called by the Name of the LORD who is enthroned between the cherubim; or the ark of God, the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim, where His Name is called

units.leftText: So they carried the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on a new cart, with Uzzah and Ahio guiding the cart. Uzzah Touches the Ark (2 Samuel 6:5–11|2SA 6:5-11*)
units.rightText: And they carried the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab: and Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.

units.leftText: David and all the Israelites were celebrating before God with all their might, with songs and on harps and lyres, with tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
units.rightText: And David and all Israel played before God with all their might, even with songs, and with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.

units.leftText: When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark, because the oxen had stumbled.
units.rightText: And when they came unto the threshing-floor of Chidon, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled.
leftNotes: 13:9 Chidon is a variant of Nacon; see 2 Samuel 6:6|2SA 6:6*.

units.leftText: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and He struck him down because he had put his hand on the ark. So he died there before God.
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put forth his hand to the ark; and there he died before God.

units.leftText: Then David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. So he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day.
units.rightText: And David was displeased, because Jehovah had broken forth upon Uzza: and he called that place Perez-uzza, unto this day.
leftNotes: 13:11 Perez-uzzah means outbreak against Uzzah.

units.leftText: That day David feared God and asked, “How can I ever bring the ark of God to me?”
units.rightText: And David was afraid of God that day, saying, How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?

units.leftText: So he did not move the ark with him to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
units.rightText: So David removed not the ark unto him into the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

units.leftText: Thus the ark of God remained with the family of Obed-edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his household and everything he owned.
units.rightText: And the ark of God remained with the family of Obed-edom in his house three months: and Jehovah blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that he had.

units.leftText: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, stonemasons, and carpenters, to build a palace for him.
units.rightText: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.

units.leftText: And David realized that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had highly exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.
units.rightText: And David perceived that Jehovah had established him king over Israel; for his kingdom was exalted on high, for his people Israel’s sake.

units.leftText: And David took more wives in Jerusalem and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And David took more wives at Jerusalem; and David begat more sons and daughters.

units.leftText: These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
units.rightText: And these are the names of the children whom he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, and Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,
leftNotes: 14:4 Shammua is a variant of Shimea; see 1 Chronicles 3:5|1CH 3:5*.

units.leftText: Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
units.rightText: and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Elpelet,

units.leftText: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
units.rightText: and Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia,

units.leftText: Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet. Two Victories over the Philistines (2 Samuel 5:17–25|2SA 5:17-25*)
units.rightText: and Elishama, and Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
leftNotes: 14:7 Beeliada is a variant of Eliada; see 2 Samuel 5:16|2SA 5:16*.

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all went in search of him; but David learned of this and went out to face them.
units.rightText: And when the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David: and David heard of it, and went out against them.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines had come and raided the Valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines had come and made a raid in the valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: So David inquired of God, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?” “Go,” replied the LORD, “for I will deliver them into your hand.”
units.rightText: And David inquired of God, saying, Shall I go up against the Philistines? and wilt thou deliver them into my hand? And Jehovah said unto him, Go up; for I will deliver them into thy hand.

units.leftText: So David and his men went up to Baal-perazim, where he defeated the Philistines and said, “Like a bursting flood, God has burst out against my enemies by my hand.” So they called that place Baal-perazim.
units.rightText: So they came up to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there; and David said, God hath broken mine enemies by my hand, like the breach of waters. Therefore they called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
leftNotes: 14:11 Baal-perazim means The Lord Bursts Out.

units.leftText: There the Philistines abandoned their gods, and David ordered that they be burned in the fire.
units.rightText: And they left their gods there; and David gave commandment, and they were burned with fire.

units.leftText: Once again the Philistines raided the valley.
units.rightText: And the Philistines yet again made a raid in the valley.

units.leftText: So David again inquired of God, who answered him, “Do not march up after them, but circle around them and attack them in front of the balsam trees.
units.rightText: And David inquired again of God; and God said unto him, Thou shalt not go up after them: turn away from them, and come upon them over against the mulberry-trees.
leftNotes: 14:14 Or aspen trees or poplar trees; also in verse 15

units.leftText: As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move out to battle, because this will mean that God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: And it shall be, when thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees, that then thou shalt go out to battle; for God is gone out before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.

units.leftText: So David did as God had commanded him, and they struck down the army of the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.
units.rightText: And David did as God commanded him: and they smote the host of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gezer.

units.leftText: And David’s fame went out into every land, and the LORD caused all nations to fear him.
units.rightText: And the fame of David went out into all lands; and Jehovah brought the fear of him upon all nations.

units.leftText: David constructed buildings for himself in the City of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
units.rightText: And David made him houses in the city of David; and he prepared a place for the ark of God, and pitched for it a tent.

units.leftText: Then David said, “No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God, because the LORD has chosen them to carry the ark of the LORD and to minister before Him forever.”
units.rightText: Then David said, None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites: for them hath Jehovah chosen to carry the ark of God, and to minister unto him for ever.

units.leftText: And David assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it.
units.rightText: And David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of Jehovah unto its place, which he had prepared for it.

units.leftText: Then he gathered together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:
units.rightText: And David gathered together the sons of Aaron, and the Levites:

units.leftText: From the Kohathites, Uriel the chief and 120 of his relatives;
units.rightText: of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brethren a hundred and twenty;

units.leftText: from the Merarites, Asaiah the chief and 220 of his relatives;
units.rightText: of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brethren two hundred and twenty;

units.leftText: from the Gershomites, Joel the chief and 130 of his relatives;
units.rightText: of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brethren a hundred and thirty;
leftNotes: 15:7 Gershomites is a variant of Gershonites; see 1 Chronicles 23:7|1CH 23:7*.

units.leftText: from the Elizaphanites, Shemaiah the chief and 200 of his relatives;
units.rightText: of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brethren two hundred;

units.leftText: from the Hebronites, Eliel the chief and 80 of his relatives;
units.rightText: of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brethren fourscore;

units.leftText: and from the Uzzielites, Amminadab the chief and 112 of his relatives.
units.rightText: of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brethren a hundred and twelve.

units.leftText: David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
units.rightText: And David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, and Joel, Shemaiah, and Eliel, and Amminadab,

units.leftText: And he said to them, “You are the heads of the Levitical families. You and your relatives must consecrate yourselves so that you may bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it.
units.rightText: and said unto them, Ye are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites: sanctify yourselves, both ye and your brethren, that ye may bring up the ark of Jehovah, the God of Israel, unto the place that I have prepared for it.

units.leftText: It was because you Levites were not with us the first time that the LORD our God burst forth in anger against us. For we did not consult Him about the proper order.” The Priests and Levites Carry the Ark
units.rightText: For because ye bare it not at the first, Jehovah our God made a breach upon us, for that we sought him not according to the ordinance.

units.leftText: So the priests and Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: And the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles, as Moses had commanded in accordance with the word of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the children of the Levites bare the ark of God upon their shoulders with the staves thereon, as Moses commanded according to the word of Jehovah.

units.leftText: David also told the leaders of the Levites to appoint their relatives as singers to lift up their voices with joy, accompanied by musical instruments— harps, lyres, and cymbals.
units.rightText: And David spake to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brethren the singers, with instruments of music, psalteries and harps and cymbals, sounding aloud and lifting up the voice with joy.

units.leftText: So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his brothers, Asaph son of Berechiah; from their brothers the Merarites, Ethan son of Kushaiah;
units.rightText: So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel; and of his brethren, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their brethren, Ethan the son of Kushaiah;

units.leftText: and with them their brothers next in rank: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-edom and Jeiel.
units.rightText: and with them their brethren of the second degree, Zechariah, Ben, and Jaaziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, Eliab, and Benaiah, and Maaseiah, and Mattithiah, and Eliphelehu, and Mikneiah, and Obed-edom, and Jeiel, the doorkeepers.
leftNotes: 15:18 Several Hebrew manuscripts and most LXX manuscripts (see also verse 20 and 1 Chronicles 16:5|1CH 16:5*); most Hebrew manuscripts Zechariah son of or Zechariah, Ben,
15:18 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah or Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Ozias

units.leftText: The musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals.
units.rightText: So the singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were appointed, with cymbals of brass to sound aloud;

units.leftText: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play the harps according to Alamoth.
units.rightText: and Zechariah, and Aziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, and Eliab, and Maaseiah, and Benaiah, with psalteries set to Alamoth;
leftNotes: 15:20 Aziel is a variant of Jaaziel; see verse 18.
15:20 Alamothis probably a musical or liturgical term; here and in Psalm 46:1|PSA 46:1*.

units.leftText: And Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to lead the music with lyres according to Sheminith.
units.rightText: and Mattithiah, and Eliphelehu, and Mikneiah, and Obed-edom, and Jeiel, and Azaziah, with harps set to the Sheminith, to lead.
leftNotes: 15:21 Sheminithis probably a musical term; here and in Psalm 6:1|PSA 6:1* and Psalm 12:1.

units.leftText: Chenaniah the head Levite was the director of the music because he was highly skilled.
units.rightText: And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the song: he instructed about the song, because he was skilful.

units.leftText: Berechiah and Elkanah were to be guardians of the ark.
units.rightText: And Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark.
leftNotes: 15:23 Literally gatekeepers; also in verse 24

units.leftText: Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer — the priests — were to blow the trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-edom and Jehiah were also to be guardians of the ark. Moving the Ark to Jerusalem
units.rightText: And Shebaniah, and Joshaphat, and Nethanel, and Amasai, and Zechariah, and Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, did blow the trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.

units.leftText: So David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with rejoicing to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom.
units.rightText: So David, and the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, went to bring up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of the house of Obed-edom with joy.

units.leftText: And because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when God helped the Levites that bare the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, that they sacrificed seven bullocks and seven rams.

units.leftText: Now David was dressed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who were carrying the ark, as well as the singers and Chenaniah, the director of music for the singers. David also wore a linen ephod.
units.rightText: And David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, and all the Levites that bare the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the master of the song with the singers: and David had upon him an ephod of linen.

units.leftText: So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouting, with the sounding of rams’ horns and trumpets, and with cymbals and the music of harps and lyres. Michal’s Contempt for David (2 Samuel 6:16|2SA 6:16*)
units.rightText: Thus all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah with shouting, and with sound of the cornet, and with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with psalteries and harps.

units.leftText: As the ark of the covenant of the LORD was entering the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from a window and saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as the ark of the covenant of Jehovah came to the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and saw king David dancing and playing; and she despised him in her heart.

units.leftText: So they brought the ark of God and placed it inside the tent that David had pitched for it. And they presented burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
units.rightText: And they brought in the ark of God, and set it in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it: and they offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before God.

units.leftText: When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
units.rightText: And when David had made an end of offering the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then he distributed to every man and woman of Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake.
units.rightText: And he dealt to every one of Israel, both man and woman, to every one a loaf of bread, and a portion of flesh, and a cake of raisins.
leftNotes: 16:3 Or a portion of meat

units.leftText: David appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to celebrate, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: And he appointed certain of the Levites to minister before the ark of Jehovah, and to celebrate and to thank and praise Jehovah, the God of Israel:

units.leftText: Asaph was the chief, Zechariah was second, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. They were to play the harps and lyres, while Asaph sounded the cymbals
units.rightText: Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, Jeiel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Mattithiah, and Eliab, and Benaiah, and Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with psalteries and with harps; and Asaph with cymbals, sounding aloud;

units.leftText: and the priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blew the trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God. David’s Psalm of Thanksgiving (Psalm 105:1–15|PSA 105:1-15*)
units.rightText: and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.

units.leftText: On that day David first committed to Asaph and his associates this song of thanksgiving to the LORD:
units.rightText: Then on that day did David first ordain to give thanks unto Jehovah, by the hand of Asaph and his brethren.

units.leftText: “Give thanks to the LORD; call upon His name; make known His deeds among the nations.
units.rightText: O give thanks unto Jehovah, call upon his name; Make known his doings among the peoples.

units.leftText: Sing to Him, sing praises to Him; tell of all His wonders.
units.rightText: Sing unto him, sing praises unto him; Talk ye of all his marvellous works.

units.leftText: Glory in His holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
units.rightText: Glory ye in his holy name; Let the heart of them rejoice that seek Jehovah.

units.leftText: Seek out the LORD and His strength; seek His face always.
units.rightText: Seek ye Jehovah and his strength; Seek his face evermore.

units.leftText: Remember the wonders He has done, His marvels, and the judgments He has pronounced,
units.rightText: Remember his marvellous works that he hath done, His wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,

units.leftText: O offspring of His servant Israel, O sons of Jacob, His chosen ones.
units.rightText: O ye seed of Israel his servant, Ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones.

units.leftText: He is the LORD our God; His judgments carry throughout the earth.
units.rightText: He is Jehovah our God; His judgments are in all the earth.

units.leftText: Remember His covenant forever, the word He ordained for a thousand generations—
units.rightText: Remember his covenant for ever, The word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
leftNotes: 16:15 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts He remembers; see Psalm 105:8|PSA 105:8*.

units.leftText: the covenant He made with Abraham, and the oath He swore to Isaac.
units.rightText: The covenant which he made with Abraham, And his oath unto Isaac,

units.leftText: He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree, to Israel as an everlasting covenant:
units.rightText: And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a statute, To Israel for an everlasting covenant,

units.leftText: ‘I will give you the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance.’
units.rightText: Saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, The lot of your inheritance;

units.leftText: When they were few in number, few indeed, and strangers in the land,
units.rightText: When ye were but a few men in number, Yea, very few, and sojourners in it;

units.leftText: they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another.
units.rightText: And they went about from nation to nation, And from one kingdom to another people.

units.leftText: He let no man oppress them; He rebuked kings on their behalf:
units.rightText: He suffered no man to do them wrong; Yea, he reproved kings for their sakes,

units.leftText: ‘Do not touch My anointed ones! Do no harm to My prophets!’ Sing to the LORD, All the Earth (Psalm 96:1–13|PSA 96:1-13*)
units.rightText: Saying, Touch not mine anointed ones, And do my prophets no harm.

units.leftText: Sing to the LORD, all the earth. Proclaim His salvation day after day.
units.rightText: Sing unto Jehovah, all the earth; Show forth his salvation from day to day.

units.leftText: Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples.
units.rightText: Declare his glory among the nations, His marvellous works among all the peoples.

units.leftText: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; He is to be feared above all gods.
units.rightText: For great is Jehovah, and greatly to be praised: He also is to be feared above all gods.

units.leftText: For all the gods of the nations are idols, but it is the LORD who made the heavens.
units.rightText: For all the gods of the peoples are idols: But Jehovah made the heavens.

units.leftText: Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and joy fill His dwelling.
units.rightText: Honor and majesty are before him: Strength and gladness are in his place.

units.leftText: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
units.rightText: Ascribe unto Jehovah, ye kindreds of the peoples, Ascribe unto Jehovah glory and strength;

units.leftText: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; bring an offering and come before Him. Worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness;
units.rightText: Ascribe unto Jehovah the glory due unto his name: Bring an offering, and come before him; Worship Jehovah in holy array.

units.leftText: tremble before Him, all the earth. The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
units.rightText: Tremble before him, all the earth: The world also is established that it cannot be moved.

units.leftText: Let the heavens be glad, and the earth rejoice. Let them say among the nations, ‘The LORD reigns!’
units.rightText: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; And let them say among the nations, Jehovah reigneth.

units.leftText: Let the sea resound, and all that fills it; let the fields exult, and all that is in them.
units.rightText: Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; Let the field exult, and all that is therein;

units.leftText: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for He is coming to judge the earth.
units.rightText: Then shall the trees of the wood sing for joy before Jehovah; For he cometh to judge the earth.

units.leftText: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.
units.rightText: O give thanks unto Jehovah; for he is good; For his lovingkindness endureth for ever.
leftNotes: 16:34 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Then cry out: ‘Save us, O God of our salvation; gather and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to Your holy name, that we may glory in Your praise.’
units.rightText: And say ye, Save us, O God of our salvation, And gather us together and deliver us from the nations, To give thanks unto thy holy name, And to triumph in thy praise.

units.leftText: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.” Then all the people said, “Amen!” and “Praise the LORD!” Worship before the Ark
units.rightText: Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, From everlasting even to everlasting. And all the people said, Amen, and praised Jehovah.

units.leftText: So David left Asaph and his associates there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to minister there regularly according to the daily requirements,
units.rightText: So he left there, before the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, Asaph and his brethren, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s work required;

units.leftText: along with Obed-edom and his sixty-eight relatives. Obed-edom son of Jeduthun, and also Hosah, were to be gatekeepers.
units.rightText: and Obed-edom with their brethren, threescore and eight; Obed-edom also the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be doorkeepers;

units.leftText: And David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon
units.rightText: and Zadok the priest, and his brethren the priests, before the tabernacle of Jehovah in the high place that was at Gibeon,

units.leftText: to regularly present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offerings, morning and evening, according to all that was written in the Law of the LORD, which He had commanded Israel to keep.
units.rightText: to offer burnt-offerings unto Jehovah upon the altar of burnt-offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is written in the law of Jehovah, which he commanded unto Israel;

units.leftText: With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, for “His loving devotion endures forever.”
units.rightText: and with them Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest that were chosen, who were mentioned by name, to give thanks to Jehovah, because his lovingkindness endureth for ever;

units.leftText: Heman and Jeduthun had with them trumpets and cymbals for the music and instruments for the songs of God. And the sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate.
units.rightText: and with them Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and with instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate.
leftNotes: 16:42 Or instruments for the sacred music

units.leftText: Then all the people departed for their homes, and David returned home to bless his household.
units.rightText: And all the people departed every man to his house: and David returned to bless his house.

units.leftText: After David had settled into his palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under a tent.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when David dwelt in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, Lo, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of Jehovah dwelleth under curtains.

units.leftText: And Nathan replied to David, “Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you.”
units.rightText: And Nathan said unto David, Do all that is in thy heart; for God is with thee.

units.leftText: But that night the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
units.rightText: And it came to pass the same night, that the word of God came to Nathan, saying,

units.leftText: “Go and tell My servant David that this is what the LORD says: You are not the one to build Me a house in which to dwell.
units.rightText: Go and tell David my servant, Thus saith Jehovah, Thou shalt not build me a house to dwell in:

units.leftText: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up out of Egypt until this day, but I have moved from tent to tent and dwelling to dwelling.
units.rightText: for I have not dwelt in a house since the day that I brought up Israel, unto this day, but have gone from tent to tent, and from one tabernacle to another.
leftNotes: 17:5 Out of Egyptis implied, but not included in the Hebrew; see 2 Samuel 7:6|2SA 7:6*.

units.leftText: In all My journeys with all the Israelites, have I ever asked any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd My people, ‘Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?’
units.rightText: In all places wherein I have walked with all Israel, spake I a word with any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people, saying, Why have ye not built me a house of cedar?
leftNotes: 17:6 Or judges; see verse 10.

units.leftText: Now then, you are to tell My servant David that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel.
units.rightText: Now therefore thus shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, that thou shouldest be prince over my people Israel:

units.leftText: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land.
units.rightText: and I have been with thee whithersoever thou hast gone, and have cut off all thine enemies from before thee; and I will make thee a name, like unto the name of the great ones that are in the earth.

units.leftText: And I will provide a place for My people Israel and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning
units.rightText: And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more; neither shall the children of wickedness waste them any more, as at the first,

units.leftText: and have done since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel. And I will subdue all your enemies.
units.rightText: and as from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel; and I will subdue all thine enemies. Moreover I tell thee that Jehovah will build thee a house.

units.leftText: And when your days are fulfilled and you go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
