units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when thy days are fulfilled that thou must go to be with thy fathers, that I will set up thy seed after thee, who shall be of thy sons; and I will establish his kingdom.

units.leftText: He will build a house for Me, and I will establish his throne forever.
units.rightText: He shall build me a house, and I will establish his throne for ever.

units.leftText: I will be his Father, and he will be My son. And I will never remove My loving devotion from him as I removed it from your predecessor.
units.rightText: I will be his father, and he shall be my son: and I will not take my lovingkindness away from him, as I took it from him that was before thee;

units.leftText: But I will set him over My house and My kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever.”
units.rightText: but I will settle him in my house and in my kingdom for ever; and his throne shall be established for ever.

units.leftText: So Nathan relayed to David all the words of this entire revelation. David’s Prayer of Thanksgiving (2 Samuel 7:18–29|2SA 7:18-29*)
units.rightText: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.

units.leftText: Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O LORD God, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
units.rightText: Then David the king went in, and sat before Jehovah; and he said, Who am I, O Jehovah God, and what is my house, that thou hast brought me thus far?

units.leftText: And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O God, You have spoken about the future of the house of Your servant and have regarded me as a man of great distinction, O LORD God.
units.rightText: And this was a small thing in thine eyes, O God; but thou hast spoken of thy servant’s house for a great while to come, and hast regarded me according to the estate of a man of high degree, O Jehovah God.
leftNotes: 17:17 Or and have shown me future generations

units.leftText: What more can David say to You for honoring Your servant? For You know Your servant,
units.rightText: What can David say yet more unto thee concerning the honor which is done to thy servant? for thou knowest thy servant.

units.leftText: O LORD. For the sake of Your servant and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing and made known all these great promises.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, for thy servant’s sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou wrought all this greatness, to make known all these great things.
leftNotes: 17:19 See 2 Samuel 7:20|2SA 7:20*; many translators 18*...For You know Your servant. 19*O LORD,

units.leftText: O LORD, there is none like You, and there is no God but You, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, there is none like thee, neither is there any God besides thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

units.leftText: And who is like Your people Israel — the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for Himself? You made a name for Yourself through great and awesome wonders by driving out nations from before Your people, whom You redeemed from Egypt.
units.rightText: And what one nation in the earth is like thy people Israel, whom God went to redeem unto himself for a people, to make thee a name by great and terrible things, in driving out nations from before thy people, whom thou redeemedst out of Egypt?

units.leftText: For You have made Your people Israel Your very own forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.
units.rightText: For thy people Israel didst thou make thine own people for ever; and thou, Jehovah, becamest their God.

units.leftText: And now, O LORD, let the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house be established forever. Do as You have promised,
units.rightText: And now, O Jehovah, let the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, be established for ever, and do as thou hast spoken.

units.leftText: so that Your name will be established and magnified forever when it is said, ‘The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, is God over Israel.’ And may the house of Your servant David be established before You.
units.rightText: And let thy name be established and magnified for ever, saying, Jehovah of hosts is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel: and the house of David thy servant is established before thee.

units.leftText: For You, my God, have revealed to Your servant that You will build a house for him. Therefore Your servant has found the courage to pray before You.
units.rightText: For thou, O my God, hast revealed to thy servant that thou wilt build him a house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray before thee.

units.leftText: And now, O LORD, You are God! And You have promised this goodness to Your servant.
units.rightText: And now, O Jehovah, thou art God, and hast promised this good thing unto thy servant:

units.leftText: So now You have been pleased to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever.”
units.rightText: and now it hath pleased thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Jehovah, hast blessed, and it is blessed for ever.

units.leftText: Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Gath and its villages from the hand of the Philistines.
units.rightText: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them, and took Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines.

units.leftText: David also defeated the Moabites, and they became subject to David and brought him tribute.
units.rightText: And he smote Moab; and the Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.

units.leftText: As far as Hamath, David also defeated King Hadadezer of Zobah, who had marched out to establish his dominion along the Euphrates River.
units.rightText: And David smote Hadarezer king of Zobah unto Hamath, as he went to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates.
leftNotes: 18:3 Hebrew his hand

units.leftText: David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and he hamstrung all the horses except a hundred he kept for the chariots.
units.rightText: And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and David hocked all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for a hundred chariots.

units.leftText: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of their men.
units.rightText: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succor Hadarezer king of Zobah, David smote of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.

units.leftText: Then he placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
units.rightText: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. And Jehovah gave victory to David whithersoever he went.
leftNotes: 18:6 LXX and Vulgate (see also 2 Samuel 8:6|2SA 8:6* and Syriac); Hebrew does not include garrisons.
18:6 Or the LORD saved David; also in verse 13

units.leftText: And David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadarezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And from Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a large amount of bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars, and various bronze articles.
units.rightText: And from Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadarezer, David took very much brass, wherewith Solomon made the brazen sea, and the pillars, and the vessels of brass.
leftNotes: 18:8 Tibhath is a variant of Tebah; see 2 Samuel 8:8|2SA 8:8* LXX.

units.leftText: When King Tou of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
units.rightText: And when Tou king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadarezer king of Zobah,
leftNotes: 18:9 Tou is a variant of Toi; also in verse 10; see 2 Samuel 8:9|2SA 8:9*.

units.leftText: he sent his son Hadoram to greet King David and bless him for fighting and defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of articles of gold and silver and bronze,
units.rightText: he sent Hadoram his son to king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadarezer and smitten him (for Hadarezer had wars with Tou); and he had with him all manner of vessels of gold and silver and brass.
leftNotes: 18:10 Hadoram is a variant of Joram; see 2 Samuel 8:10|2SA 8:10*.

units.leftText: and King David dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had carried off from all these nations — from Edom and Moab, and from the Ammonites, Philistines, and Amalekites.
units.rightText: These also did king David dedicate unto Jehovah, with the silver and the gold that he carried away from all the nations; from Edom, and from Moab, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalek.

units.leftText: Moreover, Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
units.rightText: Moreover Abishai the son of Zeruiah smote of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt eighteen thousand.

units.leftText: He placed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites were subject to David. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went. David’s Officers (2 Samuel 8:15–18|2SA 8:15-18*)
units.rightText: And he put garrisons in Edom; and all the Edomites became servants to David. And Jehovah gave victory to David whithersoever he went.

units.leftText: Thus David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people:
units.rightText: And David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness unto all his people.

units.leftText: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
units.rightText: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;

units.leftText: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was the scribe;
units.rightText: and Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abimelech the son of Abiathar, were priests; and Shavsha was scribe;
leftNotes: 18:16 Some Hebrew manuscripts, Vulgate, and Syriac (see also 2 Samuel 8:17|2SA 8:17*); most Hebrew manuscripts Abimelech
18:16 Shavsha is also called Seraiah, Sheva, and Shisha; see 2 Samuel 8:17|2SA 8:17*, 2 Samuel 20:25, and 1 Kings 4:3.

units.leftText: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief officials at the king’s side.
units.rightText: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief about the king.

units.leftText: Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after this, that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.”
units.rightText: And David said, I will show kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me. So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon to Hanun, to comfort him.

units.leftText: the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Have not his servants come to you to explore the land, spy it out, and overthrow it?”
units.rightText: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, Thinkest thou that David doth honor thy father, in that he hath sent comforters unto thee? are not his servants come unto thee to search, and to overthrow, and to spy out the land?

units.leftText: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved their beards, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.
units.rightText: So Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved them, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.

units.leftText: When someone came and told David about his men, he sent messengers to meet them, since the men had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”
units.rightText: Then there went certain persons, and told David how the men were served. And he sent to meet them; for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.

units.leftText: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
units.rightText: And when the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire them chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, and out of Aram-maacah, and out of Zobah.
leftNotes: 19:6 1,000 talents is approximately 37.7 tons or 34.2 metric tons of silver.
19:6 That is, Mesopotamia; Aram-naharaim means Aram of the two rivers, likely the region between the Euphrates and Balih Rivers in northwestern Mesopotamia.

units.leftText: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah with his troops, who came and camped near Medeba while the Ammonites were mustered from their cities and marched out for battle.
units.rightText: So they hired them thirty and two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah and his people, who came and encamped before Medeba. And the children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle.

units.leftText: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.
units.rightText: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.

units.leftText: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance to the city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country. David Defeats Ammon and Aram (2 Samuel 10:9–19|2SA 10:9-19*)
units.rightText: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the city: and the kings that were come were by themselves in the field.

units.leftText: When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.
units.rightText: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians.

units.leftText: And he placed the rest of the troops under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.
units.rightText: And the rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and they put themselves in array against the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: “If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.
units.rightText: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me; but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will help thee.

units.leftText: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”
units.rightText: Be of good courage, and let us play the man for our people, and for the cities of our God: and Jehovah do that which seemeth him good.

units.leftText: So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.
units.rightText: So Joab and the people that were with him drew nigh before the Syrians unto the battle; and they fled before him.

units.leftText: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Joab’s brother Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab went back to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.
units.rightText: And when the Syrians saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they sent messengers, and drew forth the Syrians that were beyond the River, with Shophach the captain of the host of Hadarezer at their head.
leftNotes: 19:16 Hebrew the River
19:16 Shophach is a variant of Shobach; also in verse 18; see 2 Samuel 10:16|2SA 10:16*.

units.leftText: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, advanced toward the Arameans, and arrayed for battle against them. When David lined up to engage them in battle, they fought against him.
units.rightText: And it was told David; and he gathered all Israel together, and passed over the Jordan, and came upon them, and set the battle in array against them. So when David had put the battle in array against the Syrians, they fought with him.

units.leftText: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach the commander of their army.
units.rightText: And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew of the Syrians the men of seven thousand chariots, and forty thousand footmen, and killed Shophach the captain of the host.

units.leftText: When Hadadezer’s subjects saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. So the Arameans were unwilling to help the Ammonites anymore.
units.rightText: And when the servants of Hadarezer saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they made peace with David, and served him: neither would the Syrians help the children of Ammon any more.

units.leftText: In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, Joab led out the army and ravaged the land of the Ammonites. He came to Rabbah and besieged it, but David remained in Jerusalem. And Joab attacked Rabbah and demolished it.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, at the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out to battle, that Joab led forth the army, and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried at Jerusalem. And Joab smote Rabbah, and overthrew it.
leftNotes: 20:1 Literally At the turn of the year

units.leftText: Then David took the crown from the head of their king. It was found to weigh a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David’s head. And David took a great amount of plunder from the city.
units.rightText: And David took the crown of their king from off his head, and found it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it; and it was set upon David’s head: and he brought forth the spoil of the city, exceeding much.
leftNotes: 20:2 Or from the head of Milcom. Milcom, also called Molech, was god of the Ammonites; see Leviticus 18:21|LEV 18:21* and 1 Kings 11:7.
20:2 A talent is approximately 75.4 pounds or 34.2 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. And he did the same to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem. Battles against the Philistines (2 Samuel 21:15–22|2SA 21:15-22*)
units.rightText: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and cut them with saws, and with harrows of iron, and with axes. And thus did David unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 20:3 Or cut them

units.leftText: Some time later, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were subdued.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after this, that there arose war at Gezer with the Philistines: then Sibbecai the Hushathite slew Sippai, of the sons of the giant; and they were subdued.
leftNotes: 20:4 Sippai is a variant of Saph; see 2 Samuel 21:18|2SA 21:18*.
20:4 Or the giants; see also descendants of Rapha in verses 6 and 8.

units.leftText: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
units.rightText: And there was again war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
leftNotes: 20:5 Or Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother; see 2 Samuel 21:19|2SA 21:19*.

units.leftText: And there was also a battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot— twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha,
units.rightText: And there was again war at Gath, where was a man of great stature, whose fingers and toes were four and twenty, six on each hand, and six on each foot; and he also was born unto the giant.

units.leftText: and when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David’s brother Shimei killed him.
units.rightText: And when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea David’s brother slew him.

units.leftText: So these descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants.
units.rightText: These were born unto the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.

units.leftText: Then Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel.
units.rightText: And Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel.
leftNotes: 21:1 That is, the Accuser or the Adversary

units.leftText: So David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, “Go and count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan and bring me a report, so that I may know their number.”
units.rightText: And David said to Joab and to the princes of the people, Go, number Israel from Beer-sheba even to Dan; and bring me word, that I may know the sum of them.

units.leftText: But Joab replied, “May the LORD multiply His troops a hundred times over. My lord the king, are they not all servants of my lord? Why does my lord want to do this? Why should he bring guilt on Israel?”
units.rightText: And Joab said, Jehovah make his people a hundred times as many as they are: but, my lord the king, are they not all my lord’s servants? why doth my lord require this thing? why will he be a cause of guilt unto Israel?

units.leftText: Nevertheless , the king’s word prevailed against Joab. So Joab departed and traveled throughout Israel, and then he returned to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Joab. Wherefore Joab departed, and went throughout all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And Joab reported to David the total number of the troops. In all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, including 470,000 in Judah.
units.rightText: And Joab gave up the sum of the numbering of the people unto David. And all they of Israel were a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand men that drew sword: and Judah was four hundred threescore and ten thousand men that drew sword.

units.leftText: But Joab did not include Levi and Benjamin in the count, because the king’s command was detestable to him. Judgment for David’s Sin (2 Samuel 24:10–14|2SA 24:10-14*)
units.rightText: But Levi and Benjamin counted he not among them; for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.

units.leftText: This command was also evil in the sight of God; so He struck Israel.
units.rightText: And God was displeased with this thing; therefore he smote Israel.

units.leftText: Then David said to God, “I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing. Now I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
units.rightText: And David said unto God, I have sinned greatly, in that I have done this thing: but now, put away, I beseech thee, the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.

units.leftText: And the LORD instructed Gad, David’s seer,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Gad, David’s seer, saying,

units.leftText: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”
units.rightText: Go and speak unto David, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, I offer thee three things: choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.

units.leftText: So Gad went and said to David, “This is what the LORD says: ‘You must choose
units.rightText: So Gad came to David, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Take which thou wilt:

units.leftText: between three years of famine, three months of being swept away before your enemies and overtaken by their swords, or three days of the sword of the LORD— days of plague upon the land, with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel.’ Now then, decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
units.rightText: either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before thy foes, while the sword of thine enemies overtaketh thee; or else three days the sword of Jehovah, even pestilence in the land, and the angel of Jehovah destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. Now therefore consider what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
leftNotes: 21:12 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate of fleeing; see 2 Samuel 24:13|2SA 24:13*.

units.leftText: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.” A Plague on Israel (2 Samuel 24:15–17|2SA 24:15-17*)
units.rightText: And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let me fall, I pray, into the hand of Jehovah; for very great are his mercies: and let me not fall into the hand of man.

units.leftText: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell dead.
units.rightText: So Jehovah sent a pestilence upon Israel; and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men.

units.leftText: Then God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, but as the angel was doing so, the LORD saw it and relented from the calamity, and He said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
units.rightText: And God sent an angel unto Jerusalem to destroy it: and as he was about to destroy, Jehovah beheld, and he repented him of the evil, and said to the destroying angel, It is enough; now stay thy hand. And the angel of Jehovah was standing by the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
leftNotes: 21:15 Ornan is a variant of Araunah; also in verses 18–28; see 2 Samuel 24:16|2SA 24:16*.

units.leftText: When David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem, David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.
units.rightText: And David lifted up his eyes, and saw the angel of Jehovah standing between earth and heaven, having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.

units.leftText: And David said to God, “Was it not I who gave the order to count the people? I am the one who has sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God, please let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house, but do not let this plague remain upon Your people.” David Builds an Altar (2 Samuel 24:18–25|2SA 24:18-25*)
units.rightText: And David said unto God, Is it not I that commanded the people to be numbered? even I it is that have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? let thy hand, I pray thee, O Jehovah my God, be against me, and against my father’s house; but not against thy people, that they should be plagued.
leftNotes: 21:17 Or I, the shepherd,see 2 Samuel 24:17|2SA 24:17* DSS and LXX.

units.leftText: Then the angel of the LORD ordered Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
units.rightText: Then the angel of Jehovah commanded Gad to say to David, that David should go up, and rear an altar unto Jehovah in the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

units.leftText: So David went up at the word that Gad had spoken in the name of the LORD.
units.rightText: And David went up at the saying of Gad, which he spake in the name of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now Ornan was threshing wheat when he turned and saw the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves.
units.rightText: And Ornan turned back, and saw the angel; and his four sons that were with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat.

units.leftText: David came to Ornan, and when Ornan looked out and saw David, he left the threshing floor and bowed facedown before David.
units.rightText: And as David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and went out of the threshing-floor, and bowed himself to David with his face to the ground.

units.leftText: Then David said to Ornan, “Grant me the site of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD. Sell it to me for the full price, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
units.rightText: Then David said to Ornan, Give me the place of this threshing-floor, that I may build thereon an altar unto Jehovah: for the full price shalt thou give it me, that the plague may be stayed from the people.

units.leftText: Ornan said to David, “Take it! May my lord the king do whatever seems good to him. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering— I will give it all.”
units.rightText: And Ornan said unto David, Take it to thee, and let my lord the king do that which is good in his eyes: lo, I give thee the oxen for burnt-offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meal-offering; I give it all.

units.leftText: “No,” replied King David, “I insist on paying the full price, for I will not take for the LORD what belongs to you, nor will I offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing.”
units.rightText: And king David said to Ornan, Nay; but I will verily buy it for the full price: for I will not take that which is thine for Jehovah, nor offer a burnt-offering without cost.

units.leftText: So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold for the site.
units.rightText: So David gave to Ornan for the place six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
leftNotes: 21:25 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called upon the LORD, who answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.
units.rightText: And David built there an altar unto Jehovah, and offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, and called upon Jehovah; and he answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt-offering.

units.leftText: Then the LORD spoke to the angel, who put his sword back into its sheath.
units.rightText: And Jehovah commanded the angel; and he put up his sword again into the sheath thereof.

units.leftText: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered sacrifices there.
units.rightText: At that time, when David saw that Jehovah had answered him in the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite, then he sacrificed there.

units.leftText: For the tabernacle of the LORD that Moses had made in the wilderness and the altar of burnt offering were presently at the high place in Gibeon,
units.rightText: For the tabernacle of Jehovah, which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt-offering, were at that time in the high place at Gibeon.

units.leftText: but David could not go before it to inquire of God, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.
units.rightText: But David could not go before it to inquire of God; for he was afraid because of the sword of the angel of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then David said, “Here shall be the house of the LORD God, as well as the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
units.rightText: Then David said, This is the house of Jehovah God, and this is the altar of burnt-offering for Israel.

units.leftText: So David gave orders to gather the foreigners in the land of Israel, from whom he appointed stonecutters to prepare finished stones for building the house of God.
units.rightText: And David commanded to gather together the sojourners that were in the land of Israel; and he set masons to hew wrought stones to build the house of God.

units.leftText: David provided a large quantity of iron to make the nails for the doors of the gateways and for the fittings, together with more bronze than could be weighed
units.rightText: And David prepared iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings; and brass in abundance without weight;

units.leftText: and more cedar logs than could be counted; for the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought a large quantity of cedar logs to David.
units.rightText: and cedar-trees without number: for the Sidonians and they of Tyre brought cedar-trees in abundance to David.

units.leftText: And David said, “My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent — famous and glorious throughout all lands. Therefore I must make preparations for it.” So David made lavish preparations before his death. Solomon Anointed to Build the Temple
units.rightText: And David said, Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be builded for Jehovah must be exceeding magnificent, of fame and of glory throughout all countries: I will therefore make preparation for it. So David prepared abundantly before his death.

units.leftText: Then David called for his son Solomon and instructed him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Then he called for Solomon his son, and charged him to build a house for Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: “My son,” said David to Solomon, “it was in my heart to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God,
units.rightText: And David said to Solomon his son, As for me, it was in my heart to build a house unto the name of Jehovah my God.

units.leftText: but this word of the LORD came to me: ‘You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You are not to build a house for My Name because you have shed so much blood on the ground before Me.
units.rightText: But the word of Jehovah came to me, saying, Thou hast shed blood abundantly, and hast made great wars: thou shalt not build a house unto my name, because thou hast shed much blood upon the earth in my sight.

units.leftText: But a son will be born to you who will be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side; for his name will be Solomon, and I will grant to Israel peace and quiet during his reign.
units.rightText: Behold, a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about; for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.
leftNotes: 22:9 Solomon sounds like and is probably derived from the Hebrew word for peace.

units.leftText: He is the one who will build a house for My Name. He will be My son, and I will be his Father. And I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’
units.rightText: He shall build a house for my name; and he shall be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.

units.leftText: Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, and may you succeed in building the house of the LORD your God, as He said you would.
units.rightText: Now, my son, Jehovah be with thee; and prosper thou, and build the house of Jehovah thy God, as he hath spoken concerning thee.

units.leftText: Above all, may the LORD give you insight and understanding when He puts you in command over Israel, so that you may keep the Law of the LORD your God.
units.rightText: Only Jehovah give thee discretion and understanding, and give thee charge concerning Israel; that so thou mayest keep the law of Jehovah thy God.

units.leftText: Then you will succeed, if you carefully follow the statutes and ordinances that the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou prosper, if thou observe to do the statutes and the ordinances which Jehovah charged Moses with concerning Israel: be strong, and of good courage; fear not, neither be dismayed.

units.leftText: Now behold, I have taken great pains to provide for the house of the LORD— 100,000 talents of gold, 1,000,000 talents of silver, and bronze and iron too great to be weighed. I have also provided timber and stone, and you may add to them.
units.rightText: Now, behold, in my affliction I have prepared for the house of Jehovah a hundred thousand talents of gold, and a thousand thousand talents of silver, and of brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance: timber also and stone have I prepared; and thou mayest add thereto.
leftNotes: 22:14 100,000 talents is approximately 3,770 tons or 3,420 metric tons of gold.
22:14 1,000,000 talents is approximately 37,700 tons or 34,200 metric tons of silver.

units.leftText: You also have many workers: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and men skilled in every kind of work —
units.rightText: Moreover there are workmen with thee in abundance, hewers and workers of stone and timber, and all men that are skilful in every manner of work:

units.leftText: in gold and silver, bronze and iron— craftsmen beyond number. Now begin the work, and may the LORD be with you.”
units.rightText: of the gold, the silver, and the brass, and the iron, there is no number. Arise and be doing, and Jehovah be with thee.

units.leftText: Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon:
units.rightText: David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,

units.leftText: “Is not the LORD your God with you, and has He not granted you rest on every side? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before the LORD and His people.
units.rightText: Is not Jehovah your God with you? and hath he not given you rest on every side? for he hath delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand; and the land is subdued before Jehovah, and before his people.

units.leftText: Now set your heart and soul to seek the LORD your God. Begin building the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles of God into the temple that will be built for the Name of the LORD.”
units.rightText: Now set your heart and your soul to seek after Jehovah your God; arise therefore, and build ye the sanctuary of Jehovah God, to bring the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, and the holy vessels of God, into the house that is to be built to the name of Jehovah.

units.leftText: When David was old and full of years, he installed his son Solomon as king over Israel.
units.rightText: Now David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.

units.leftText: Then he gathered all the leaders of Israel, as well as the priests and Levites.
units.rightText: And he gathered together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.

units.leftText: The Levites thirty years of age or older were counted, and the total number of men was 38,000.
units.rightText: And the Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward: and their number by their polls, man by man, was thirty and eight thousand.

units.leftText: “Of these,” said David, “24,000 are to oversee the work of the house of the LORD, 6,000 are to be officers and judges,
units.rightText: Of these, twenty and four thousand were to oversee the work of the house of Jehovah; and six thousand were officers and judges;
leftNotes: 23:4 Hebrew does not include said David,

units.leftText: 4,000 are to be gatekeepers, and 4,000 are to praise the LORD with the instruments I have made for giving praise.”
units.rightText: and four thousand were doorkeepers; and four thousand praised Jehovah with the instruments which I made, said David, to praise therewith.

units.leftText: Then David divided the Levites into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. The Gershonites (Numbers 3:21–26|NUM 3:21-26*; Numbers 4:21–28|NUM 4:21-28*)
units.rightText: And David divided them into courses according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

units.leftText: The Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
units.rightText: Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
leftNotes: 23:7 Ladan is a variant of Libni; also in verses 8 and 9; see 1 Chronicles 6:17|1CH 6:17*.

units.leftText: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the first, Zetham, and Joel— three in all.
units.rightText: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, and Zetham, and Joel, three.
leftNotes: 23:8 Jehiel is a variant of Jehieli; see 1 Chronicles 26:21|1CH 26:21*.

units.leftText: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran— three in all. These were the heads of the families of Ladan.
units.rightText: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, and Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ houses of Ladan.

units.leftText: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei— four in all.
units.rightText: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, and Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
leftNotes: 23:10 Shimei was possibly a son or grandson of the Shimei listed in verse 9.
23:10 Most Hebrew manuscripts; one Hebrew manuscript, LXX, and Vulgate (see also verse 11) Zizah

units.leftText: Jahath was the first and Zizah was the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one family and received a single assignment. The Kohathites (Numbers 3:27–32|NUM 3:27-32*; Numbers 4:1–20|NUM 4:1-20*)
units.rightText: And Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second: but Jeush and Beriah had not many sons; therefore they became a fathers’ house in one reckoning.

units.leftText: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel— four in all.
units.rightText: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.

units.leftText: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister before Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name forever.
units.rightText: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron was separated, that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons, for ever, to burn incense before Jehovah, to minister unto him, and to bless in his name, for ever.

units.leftText: As for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
units.rightText: But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.

units.leftText: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
units.rightText: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

units.leftText: The descendants of Gershom: Shebuel was the first.
units.rightText: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.

units.leftText: The descendants of Eliezer: Rehabiah was the first. Eliezer did not have any other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very numerous.
units.rightText: And the sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.

units.leftText: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith was the first.
units.rightText: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.

units.leftText: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah was the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
units.rightText: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.

units.leftText: The sons of Uzziel: Micah was the first and Isshiah the second. The Merarites (Numbers 3:33–37|NUM 3:33-37*; Numbers 4:29–33|NUM 4:29-33*)
units.rightText: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.

units.leftText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.
units.rightText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.

units.leftText: Eleazar died without having any sons; he had only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.
units.rightText: And Eleazar died, and had no sons, but daughters only: and their brethren the sons of Kish took them to wife.

units.leftText: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth — three in all. Levite Duties Revised
units.rightText: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, and Eder, and Jeremoth, three.
leftNotes: 23:23 Jeremoth is a variant of Jerimoth; see 1 Chronicles 24:30|1CH 24:30*.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Levi by their families— the heads of families, registered individually by name— those twenty years of age or older who worked in the service of the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of those of them that were counted, in the number of names by their polls, who did the work for the service of the house of Jehovah, from twenty years old and upward.

units.leftText: For David had said, “The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people and has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever.
units.rightText: For David said, Jehovah, the God of Israel, hath given rest unto his people; and he dwelleth in Jerusalem for ever:

units.leftText: So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service.”
units.rightText: and also the Levites shall no more have need to carry the tabernacle and all the vessels of it for the service thereof.

units.leftText: For according to the final instructions of David, the Levites twenty years of age or older were counted,
units.rightText: For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were numbered, from twenty years old and upward.

units.leftText: but their duty was to assist the descendants of Aaron with the service of the house of the LORD, being responsible for the courts and chambers, the purification of all the holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God,
units.rightText: For their office was to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of Jehovah, in the courts, and in the chambers, and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of the house of God;

units.leftText: as well as for the rows of the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size.
units.rightText: for the showbread also, and for the fine flour for a meal-offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all manner of measure and size;

units.leftText: They were also to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening.
units.rightText: and to stand every morning to thank and praise Jehovah, and likewise at even;

units.leftText: Whenever burnt offerings were presented to the LORD on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed feasts, they were to serve regularly before the LORD in the numbers prescribed for them.
units.rightText: and to offer all burnt-offerings unto Jehovah, on the sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, in number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before Jehovah;

units.leftText: So the Levites were to carry out the responsibilities for the Tent of Meeting and the Holy Place, and, under their brothers the descendants of Aaron, the service of the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: and that they should keep the charge of the tent of meeting, and the charge of the holy place, and the charge of the sons of Aaron their brethren, for the service of the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: These were the divisions of the descendants of Aaron. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
units.rightText: And the courses of the sons of Aaron were these. The sons of Aaron: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

units.leftText: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father did, and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
units.rightText: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and had no children: therefore Eleazar and Ithamar executed the priest’s office.

units.leftText: With the help of Eleazar’s descendant Zadok and Ithamar’s descendant Ahimelech, David divided them according to the offices of their service.
units.rightText: And David with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar, and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their ordering in their service.

units.leftText: Since more leaders were found among Eleazar’s descendants than those of Ithamar, they were divided accordingly. There were sixteen heads of families from the descendants of Eleazar and eight from the descendants of Ithamar.
units.rightText: And there were more chief men found of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar; and thus were they divided: of the sons of Eleazar there were sixteen, heads of fathers’ houses; and of the sons of Ithamar, according to their fathers’ houses, eight.

units.leftText: Thus they were divided by lot, for there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both Eleazar’s and Ithamar’s descendants.
units.rightText: Thus were they divided by lot, one sort with another; for there were princes of the sanctuary, and princes of God, both of the sons of Eleazar, and of the sons of Ithamar.

units.leftText: The scribe, Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite, recorded their names in the presence of the king and of the officers: Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of families of the priests and the Levites — one family being taken from Eleazar, and then one from Ithamar.
units.rightText: And Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, who was of the Levites, wrote them in the presence of the king, and the princes, and Zadok the priest, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the priests and of the Levites; one fathers’ house being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar.

units.leftText: The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
units.rightText: Now the first lot came forth to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,

units.leftText: the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
units.rightText: the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,

units.leftText: the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
units.rightText: the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,

units.leftText: the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
units.rightText: the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,

units.leftText: the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
units.rightText: the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,

units.leftText: the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
units.rightText: the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,

units.leftText: the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
units.rightText: the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,

units.leftText: the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
units.rightText: the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,

units.leftText: the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
units.rightText: the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,

units.leftText: the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
units.rightText: the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,

units.leftText: the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
units.rightText: the one and twentieth to Jachin, the two and twentieth to Gamul,

units.leftText: the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
units.rightText: the three and twentieth to Delaiah, the four and twentieth to Maaziah.

units.leftText: This was their appointed order for service when they entered the house of the LORD, according to the regulations prescribed for them by their forefather Aaron, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him. The Rest of the Levites
units.rightText: This was the ordering of them in their service, to come into the house of Jehovah according to the ordinance given unto them by Aaron their father, as Jehovah, the God of Israel, had commanded him.

units.leftText: Now these were the rest of the descendants of Levi: From the sons of Amram: Shubael; from the sons of Shubael: Jehdeiah.
units.rightText: And of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
leftNotes: 24:20 Shubael (twice in this verse) is a variant of Shebuel; see 1 Chronicles 23:16|1CH 23:16* and 1 Chronicles 26:24.

units.leftText: As for Rehabiah, from his sons: The first was Isshiah.
units.rightText: Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
leftNotes: 24:21 Isshiah is a variant of Jeshaiah; see 1 Chronicles 26:25|1CH 26:25*.

units.leftText: From the Izharites: Shelomoth; from the sons of Shelomoth: Jahath.
units.rightText: Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
leftNotes: 24:22 Shelomoth (twice in this verse) is a variant of Shelomith; see 1 Chronicles 23:18|1CH 23:18*.

units.leftText: From the sons of Hebron: Jeriah was the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
units.rightText: And the sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
leftNotes: 24:23 Hebrew From the sons: Jeriah; see 1 Chronicles 23:19|1CH 23:19*.

units.leftText: From the sons of Uzziel: Micah; from the sons of Micah: Shamir.
units.rightText: The sons of Uzziel, Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.

units.leftText: The brother of Micah: Isshiah; from the sons of Isshiah: Zechariah.
units.rightText: The brother of Micah, Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.

units.leftText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno.
units.rightText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; the sons of Jaaziah: Beno.

units.leftText: The descendants of Merari from Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
units.rightText: The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno, and Shoham, and Zaccur, and Ibri.

units.leftText: From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
units.rightText: Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.

units.leftText: From Kish: Jerahmeel the son of Kish.
units.rightText: Of Kish; the sons of Kish: Jerahmeel.

units.leftText: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
units.rightText: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, and Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after their fathers’ houses.
leftNotes: 24:30 Jerimoth is a variant of Jeremoth; see 1 Chronicles 23:23|1CH 23:23*.

units.leftText: As their brothers the descendants of Aaron did, they also cast lots in the presence of King David and of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites— the family heads and their younger brothers alike.
units.rightText: These likewise cast lots even as their brethren the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, and Zadok, and Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the priests and of the Levites; the fathers’ houses of the chief even as those of his younger brother.

units.leftText: Additionally, David and the commanders of the army set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to prophesy with the accompaniment of lyres, harps, and cymbals. The following is the list of the men who performed this service:
units.rightText: Moreover David and the captains of the host set apart for the service certain of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals: and the number of them that did the work according to their service was:

units.leftText: From the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah. These sons of Asaph were under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the direction of the king.
units.rightText: of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, and Joseph, and Nethaniah, and Asharelah, the sons of Asaph, under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied after the order of the king.

units.leftText: From the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah , Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah — six in all — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
units.rightText: Of Jeduthun; the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, and Zeri, and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of their father Jeduthun with the harp, who prophesied in giving thanks and praising Jehovah.
leftNotes: 25:3 One Hebrew manuscript and some LXX manuscripts (see also verse 17); most Hebrew manuscripts do not include Shimei.

units.leftText: From the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
units.rightText: Of Heman; the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
leftNotes: 25:4 Shebuel is a variant of Shubael; see verse 20.
25:4 Jerimoth is a variant of Jeremoth; see verse 22.

units.leftText: All these sons of Heman the king’s seer were given him through the promises of God to exalt him, for God had given Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
units.rightText: All these were the sons of Heman the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. And God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

units.leftText: All these were under the direction of their fathers for the music of the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God.
units.rightText: All these were under the hands of their father for song in the house of Jehovah, with cymbals, psalteries, and harps, for the service of the house of God; Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman being under the order of the king.

units.leftText: Together with their relatives, who were all trained and skillful in the songs of the LORD, they numbered 288.
units.rightText: And the number of them, with their brethren that were instructed in singing unto Jehovah, even all that were skilful, was two hundred fourscore and eight.

units.leftText: They cast lots for their duties, young and old alike, teacher as well as pupil.
units.rightText: And they cast lots for their offices, all alike, as well the small as the great, the teacher as the scholar.

units.leftText: The first lot, which was for Asaph, fell to Joseph, his sons, and his brothers—12 in all; the second to Gedaliah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: Now the first lot came forth for Asaph to Joseph: the second to Gedaliah; he and his brethren and sons were twelve:
leftNotes: 25:9 See LXX and the total in verse 7; Hebrew does not include his sons, and his brothers—12 in all;

units.leftText: the third to Zaccur, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the fourth to Izri, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brethren, twelve:
leftNotes: 25:11 Izri is a variant of Zeri; see verse 3.

units.leftText: the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the seventh to Jesarelah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:
leftNotes: 25:14 Jesarelah is a variant of Asarelah; see verse 2.

units.leftText: the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the tenth to Shimei, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the eleventh to Azarel, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brethren, twelve:
leftNotes: 25:18 Azarel is a variant of Uzziel; see verse 4.

units.leftText: the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the thirteenth to Shubael, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brethren, twelve:
leftNotes: 25:22 Jeremoth is a variant of Jerimoth; see verse 4.

units.leftText: the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the one and twentieth to Hothir, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the two and twentieth to Giddalti, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
units.rightText: for the three and twentieth to Mahazioth, his sons and his brethren, twelve:

units.leftText: and the twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all.
units.rightText: for the four and twentieth to Romamtiezer, his sons and his brethren, twelve.

units.leftText: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites: Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.
units.rightText: For the courses of the doorkeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.

units.leftText: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
units.rightText: And Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the first-born, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,

units.leftText: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
units.rightText: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.

units.leftText: And Obed-edom also had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
units.rightText: And Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the first-born, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, and Sacar the fourth, and Nethanel the fifth,

units.leftText: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth. For God had blessed Obed-edom.
units.rightText: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.

units.leftText: Also to his son Shemaiah were born sons who ruled over their families because they were strong, capable men.
units.rightText: Also unto Shemaiah his son were sons born, that ruled over the house of their father; for they were mighty men of valor.

units.leftText: Shemaiah’s sons were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad; his brothers were Elihu and Semachiah, also capable men.
units.rightText: The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad, whose brethren were valiant men, Elihu, and Semachiah.

units.leftText: All these were descendants of Obed-edom; they and their sons and brothers were capable men with strength to do the work— 62 in all from Obed-edom.
units.rightText: All these were of the sons of Obed-edom: they and their sons and their brethren, able men in strength for the service; threescore and two of Obed-edom.

units.leftText: Meshelemiah also had sons and brothers who were capable men— 18 in all.
units.rightText: And Meshelemiah had sons and brethren, valiant men, eighteen.

units.leftText: Hosah the Merarite also had sons: Shimri the first (although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him as the first),
units.rightText: Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the first-born, yet his father made him chief),

units.leftText: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. The sons and brothers of Hosah numbered 13 in all.
units.rightText: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brethren of Hosah were thirteen.

units.leftText: These divisions of the gatekeepers, through their chief men, had duties for ministering in the house of the LORD, just as their relatives did.
units.rightText: Of these were the courses of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men, having offices like their brethren, to minister in the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: They cast lots for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike.
units.rightText: And they cast lots, as well the small as the great, according to their fathers’ houses, for every gate.

units.leftText: The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and the lot for the North Gate fell to him.
units.rightText: And the lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a discreet counsellor, they cast lots; and his lot came out northward.
leftNotes: 26:14 Shelemiah is a variant of Meshelemiah; see verse 2.

units.leftText: The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-edom, and the lot for the storehouses to his sons.
units.rightText: To Obed-edom southward; and to his sons the store-house.

units.leftText: The lots for the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the ascending highway fell to Shuppim and Hosah.
units.rightText: To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goeth up, watch against watch.
leftNotes: 26:16 Or on the upper road

units.leftText: Each day there were six Levites on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two pairs at the storehouse.
units.rightText: Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the store-house two and two.

units.leftText: As for the court on the west, there were four at the highway and two at the court.
units.rightText: For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
leftNotes: 26:18 Hebrew parbar; twice in this verse

units.leftText: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers who were descendants of Korah and Merari. The Treasurers, Officers, and Judges
units.rightText: These were the courses of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.

units.leftText: Now their fellow Levites were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things.
units.rightText: And of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of the house of God, and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
leftNotes: 26:20 LXX; Hebrew As for the Levites, Ahijah was

units.leftText: From the descendants of Ladan, who were Gershonites through Ladan and heads of the families of Ladan the Gershonite, were Jehieli,
units.rightText: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
leftNotes: 26:21 Ladan is a variant of Libni; see 1 Chronicles 6:17|1CH 6:17*.
26:21 Jehieli is a variant of Jehiel; also in verse 22; see 1 Chronicles 23:8|1CH 23:8*.

units.leftText: the sons of Jehieli, Zetham, and his brother Joel. They were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: From the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
units.rightText: Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:

units.leftText: Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the officer in charge of the treasuries.
units.rightText: and Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasures.

units.leftText: His relatives through Eliezer included Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.
units.rightText: And his brethren: of Eliezer came Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.
leftNotes: 26:25 Jeshaiah is a variant of Isshiah; see 1 Chronicles 24:21|1CH 24:21*.

units.leftText: This Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries for the things dedicated by King David, by the heads of families who were the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and by the army commanders.
units.rightText: This Shelomoth and his brethren were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ houses, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the host, had dedicated.

units.leftText: They had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to the repair of the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: Out of the spoil won in battles did they dedicate to repair the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Everything that had been dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah, along with everything else that was dedicated, was under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.
units.rightText: And all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated, whosoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth, and of his brethren.

units.leftText: From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons had the outside duties as officers and judges over Israel.
units.rightText: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.
leftNotes: 26:29 Or the duties outside (the temple) or the duties outside (Jerusalem)

units.leftText: From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives, 1,700 capable men, had charge of the affairs of Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.
units.rightText: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valor, a thousand and seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Jehovah, and for the service of the king.

units.leftText: As for the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to the genealogies of his ancestors. In the fortieth year of David’s reign the records were searched, and strong, capable men were found among the Hebronites at Jazer in Gilead.
units.rightText: Of the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ houses. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought for, and there were found among them mighty men of valor at Jazer of Gilead.
leftNotes: 26:31 Jerijah is a variant of Jeriah; see 1 Chronicles 23:19|1CH 23:19*.

units.leftText: Among Jerijah’s relatives there were 2,700 capable men who were heads of families. King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.
units.rightText: And his brethren, men of valor, were two thousand and seven hundred, heads of fathers’ houses, whom king David made overseers over the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God, and for the affairs of the king.

units.leftText: This is the list of the Israelites— the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter concerning the divisions on rotating military duty each month throughout the year. There were 24,000 men in each division:
units.rightText: Now the children of Israel after their number, to wit, the heads of fathers’ houses and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers that served the king, in any matter of the courses which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—of every course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was in charge of the first division, which was assigned the first month. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: Over the first course for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: He was a descendant of Perez and chief of all the army commanders for the first month.
units.rightText: He was of the children of Perez, the chief of all the captains of the host for the first month.

units.leftText: Dodai the Ahohite was in charge of the division for the second month, and Mikloth was the leader. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: And over the course of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and his course; and Mikloth the ruler: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.
leftNotes: 27:4 Dodai is a variant of Dodo; see 2 Samuel 23:9|2SA 23:9*.

units.leftText: The third army commander, as chief for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The third captain of the host for the third month was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the priest, chief: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: This Benaiah was mighty among the Thirty and was over the Thirty, and his son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.
units.rightText: This is that Benaiah, who was the mighty man of the thirty, and over the thirty: and of his course was Ammizabad his son.

units.leftText: The fourth, for the fourth month, was Joab’s brother Asahel, and his son Zebadiah was commander after him. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The fourth captain for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The fifth captain for the fifth month was Shamhuth the Izrahite: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.
leftNotes: 27:8 Shamhuth is a variant of Shammoth or Shammah; see 1 Chronicles 11:27|1CH 11:27* and 2 Samuel 23:25.

units.leftText: The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The sixth captain for the sixth month was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, an Ephraimite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The seventh captain for the seventh month was Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The eighth captain for the eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjamite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The ninth captain for the ninth month was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The tenth captain for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, an Ephraimite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
units.rightText: The eleventh captain for the eleventh month was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel. There were 24,000 men in his division. The Leaders of the Twelve Tribes
units.rightText: The twelfth captain for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.
leftNotes: 27:15 Heldai is a variant of Heled; see 1 Chronicles 11:30|1CH 11:30* and 2 Samuel 23:29.

units.leftText: These officers were in charge of the tribes of Israel: Over the Reubenites was Eliezer son of Zichri; over the Simeonites was Shephatiah son of Maacah;
units.rightText: Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites was Eliezer the son of Zichri the ruler: of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah:

units.leftText: over Levi was Hashabiah son of Kemuel; over Aaron was Zadok;
units.rightText: of Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel: of Aaron, Zadok:

units.leftText: over Judah was Elihu, one of David’s brothers; over Issachar was Omri son of Michael;
units.rightText: of Judah, Elihu, one of the brethren of David: of Issachar, Omri the son of Michael:

units.leftText: over Zebulun was Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; over Naphtali was Jerimoth son of Azriel;
units.rightText: of Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah: of Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel:

units.leftText: over the Ephraimites was Hoshea son of Azaziah; over one of the half-tribes of Manasseh was Joel son of Pedaiah;
